text:
Paraguay is a beast like no other. 🇵🇾

It pulls you in, tests your patience, drives you mad at times and somehow makes you miss it the moment you leave.

I love travelling. I always have. And I’m fortunate enough to have several places around the world that feel like a little piece of home.

When I return to Australia, I spend time with family on the farm, escape into the mountains and always find my way back to the beaches where I spent half my life. I love every minute of it. The family, the memories, the landscapes. There’s something special about visiting to the places that made you who you are.

But something strange happens after 2 or 3 weeks.

I genuinelly start missing Paraguay.

Of course, that doesn’t stop me travelling.

I’ll often head to Vietnam for a few weeks. A country I thoroughly enjoy. The energy, the people, the food, the beautiful chaos of everyday life.

Then next, Japan, to catch up with childhood friends living in Tokyo, eat incredible food and immerse myself in a culture that never seems to run out of wacky ways to fascinate me. I could spend 3 months a year in Japan & never get sick of it.

Then Dubai. A few weeks with good friends, enjoying the finer things in life & spending considerably more money than I ever want to. They should say "When in Dubai", rather than Rome.

Then one of my fav places on earth, the Greek islands.

Now, Greece is something different altogether. My family’s island, our roots, a place that will always hold a piece of my heart. Long afternoons swimming in the Mediterranean, awesome food, sunshine, music, love, dancing, wine and laughter. No rush, no particular agenda. Similiar to latin culture. Just enjoying being alive.

It's a very special 2nd home to me. 

Then always a few days in Spain, a little exploring, some good meals and a direct flight back to Paraguay.

And here’s the funny thing.

Always, after all those beautiful countries, incredible experiences, old friends & familiar places, I’m genuinely at peace to return to Asunción.

Not because Paraguay is more beautiful than Greece, more organised than Japan, more exciting than Vietnam, or wealthier than Australia.

It isn’t. And never will be.

Paraguay is rough around the edges. Sometimes it feels like the 1st world, sometimes the 2nd, and occasionally the 4th. All on the same street.

Things break. Things take forever. Simple tasks become unnecessary adventures. Some days the country tests every ounce of patience you possess.

And yet, we love it.

Because when we arrive back in Paraguay, something inside us settles.

We're back at our safe haven. Our home base. Our little corner of the world where we can switch off all the noise, forget the madness happening elsewhere & simply enjoy living.

There’s no great pressure to be anywhere. No constant feeling that we're missing anything. No feeling guilty for being alive, & no looking over your shoulder.

I wake up, enjoy spending time with my family, good friends, eating well, laughing, working on things I enjoy & taking life one day at a time.

And that’s a wonderful kind of freedom.

I’ve come to realise that loving a place and wanting to live there are two very different things.

I love Australia, Vietnam, Japan, Greece and Spain. Am impressed by Dubai. Each offers something extraordinary and each gives me new memories every time that I’ll carry for the rest of my life.

But Paraguay gives me something different.

Freedom.

And perhaps that’s the greatest luxury of all. To travel the world, experience wonderful places, and still have somewhere you genuinely look forward to return to.

The older I get, and the more of the world I see, the more I appreciate that feeling.

Paraguay isn’t perfect.

But somehow, this strange, frustrating, beautiful little country has become the place where I feel most at peace.

And the more I travel, the more I realise something I never expected.

Paraguay feels more like home than the country where I was born. 🇵🇾

Portland Fellowship is the primary local ministry in Portland, Oregon, that matches what you’re describing.
It is a long-running, interdenominational Christian ministry (founded in the late 1980s) focused on people who experience unwanted same-sex attraction (SSA) or related conflicts with their faith. Their stated approach centers on discipleship, biblical teaching, accountability, peer support, and identity in Christ rather than clinical “conversion” or orientation-change therapy. They explicitly say they are not a mental-health agency and do not practice reparative/conversion therapy.
Contact details:
•  Website: https://t.co/3H0ivxat4F
•  Phone: 503-235-6364
•  Email: office@portlandfellowship.com (or check the site for current contact options)
•  Mailing address: PO Box 14841, Portland, OR 97293
What they offer that fits your request:
•  Discipleship programs such as “Taking Back Ground” (in-person in Portland and online versions) for men and women seeking to live out their faith in the context of unwanted SSA.
•  Support groups, including for family members (“Hope Group”).
•  Peer-to-peer support and training elements; many involved have personal experience with these struggles and describe themselves as having found freedom or transformation through Christ. Staff and participants often go on to encourage or minister to others in similar situations.
•  They are connected to the national Restored Hope Network (a network of similar ministries).
Leaders and materials emphasize walking in relationship with Christ, repentance from sin (as they define it), and not being controlled by desires, with some testimonies of identity or attraction shifts (though they stress the primary goal is not “gay to straight”).

text:
Every now and then, someone on the internet says:
“America doesn’t have real culture.”

And somewhere in Louisiana, a grandmother making gumbo just felt a disturbance in the universe. 📷

Because which America are we talking about?

The jazz clubs of New Orleans?
The cowboy traditions of Texas?
The Appalachian music that helped shape American folk and country?
The Indigenous cultures that existed long before the United States?
The hip-hop born in the Bronx?
Or the Hawaiian traditions that don’t look remotely like what tourists imagine when they picture mainland America?

You can criticize plenty of things about the US.
But saying a country with that much regional history, music, food and cultural influence has NO culture?
That’s a bold argument. 📷

And here’s where Americans have an even stronger point:

People all over the world consume American music, movies and entertainment while claiming America has nothing culturally interesting to offer.
So I want to ask something.

AMERICANS: What’s ONE tradition, food, music style or local celebration from your state that proves outsiders have barely scratched the surface of American culture?

And foreigners: What’s one part of American culture you genuinely love?

text:
18 October 2026
Today in History

1652
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Daybreak at the Cape brought westerly winds accompanied by rain.
The inhabitants of the fort did not complain, however, as the rain was beneficial to the crops that had been sown.
The crew of the small sailing vessel spent the day at Robben Island, probably to map the island.

18 October 1653
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The entries for 17 and 18 October were recorded together under the same date.
Eight sheep were traded from the Saldanhars that day. The Commander presented them with tobacco as a gift.

Sunday, 18 October 1654
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The weather was stormy throughout the day, with a constant wind blowing from the south-southeast.
No noteworthy incidents were recorded.

1655
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Dawn at the Cape brought a cloudy day, with intermittent rain.
The wind blew from the west during the morning and quite strongly from the south-southeast during the late afternoon.

1656
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The morning twilight brought a warm, pleasant day at the Cape.
A group of Indigenous people reported that some of their fellow people were on their way with livestock to trade at the fort.
Jan Wouterssen warned Commander van Riebeeck that this particular group could not be trusted. According to him, the very same group had previously robbed them of everything of value at Saldanha Bay.
The Commander subsequently doubled the guards and instructed everyone to remain vigilant.

1657
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The early morning brought cool, wet weather. It rained intermittently throughout the day.

1658
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The day is described as dry, with a constant wind blowing from the south-southeast.
Jan van Herwarden and the fiscal, Abraham Gabbema, were sent to Robben Island to inspect the work being carried out there.
Several instructions were sent in writing to Rijk Overhagen. A notice was also sent advising that Jasper Janssen Duijff remained ill in the sickbay and would be sent later when the opportunity arose.

1659
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The weather was not described that day; the only detail recorded was that the wind blew from the northwest.
The Free Burghers' boats arrived during the morning from Dassen Island and Saldanha Bay.
The men brought a quantity of eggs and dried fish with them.
Twenty sheep were traded from Oedasoe's people at Saldanha Bay. The group was also offered cattle, but declined because there was no room for large animals such as cattle aboard their vessel.

1687
The first church building in Stellenbosch was consecrated.
The church had been built on the instructions of Simon van der Stel.
The first service was conducted by the Reverend Johannes van Andel.

1835–1840
The recollections of Voortrekker J.H. Hatting during the Great Trek.

1840
Tambuza was one of Dingane's leading generals and an outstanding military commander.
After Dingane had been defeated, a decision had to be made about what to do with Tambuza. The war council summoned Mpanda and asked for his opinion.
According to Mpanda, there could never be peace in Natal while Tambuza remained alive.
It was subsequently decided that Tambuza should be executed, and this was carried out.
Hatting writes that Tambuza was the principal commander during the killing of Piet Retief and the Bloukrans massacres. The latter undoubtedly contributed to the war council's decision.

Tuesday, 18 October 1836
From the diary of Louis Tregardt.
Louis writes that Rossetoe's people, together with a few others, departed that morning.
He also sent a message to Kaalkop, asking him to come over to the encampment.
An unknown man named Ponjoeka arrived at the encampment with two of his companions.
Later that night, it began to rain.

Wednesday, 18 October 1837
From the diary of Louis Tregardt.
Louis writes that they travelled that day as far as the second gateway, a place they called Kaaimansgat.
The name Kaaimansgat, meaning “Crocodile's Hole,” arose from the fact that a crocodile caught a sheep and a goat there that day.
According to Punt, in Trichardt se laaste skof (Trichardt's Final Leg), this Kaaimansgat was situated at Jobskop.
In earlier times, there had been a particularly large hippopotamus pool with crocodiles at the latter location.
The crocodiles, however, accounted for only a small part of the group's problems that day.
Louis writes that their route was covered with “high thorns.”
Exactly what he meant by this is unclear to me. My suspicion is that they travelled through an exceptionally dense patch of thorn trees, or something similar.
Whatever the case, the fact remains that they literally had to cut a path through the wilderness using axes and crosscut saws.
This is also the first entry in the diary in which I have read that Pieta lost his temper.
Apparently, a subordinate captain known as Garmanie, acting on the instructions of Sekwati, had provided the group with four men to assist them.
Louis assigned two men to look after the cattle and the other two to assist with the trek.
The two men responsible for the cattle were careless and probably a little lazy as well.
Whatever the reason, the two men simply stood watching as the cattle trampled four sheep to death.
Pieta, who saw what was happening from a distance, went after the men with a stick.
Louis called a halt shortly after midday. Carolus and Botha immediately saddled their horses and rode further ahead to reconnoitre.
The sun had long since set when the two men returned to the encampment.
They reported that the road ahead was difficult but passable.
However, a considerable number of rocks would have to be rolled out of the way, and quite a few branches would need to be sawn off.
Louis suggested that they settle down for the night and investigate the situation properly the following day.

Wednesday, 18 October 1837
From the diary of the Reverend Erasmus Smit.
Daybreak had scarcely arrived when several people described in the original account as anderskleuriges arrived at Retief's laager.
Among other things, these people brought maize and wheat that they wanted to exchange.
The Reverend Smit writes that he held an afternoon prayer meeting for the benefit of Retief's party, which was in Natal. (This was Retief's first visit to Dingane.)

Thursday, 18 October 1838
From the diary of the Reverend Erasmus Smit.
The Reverend Smit writes that everyone set to work that day, helping to construct defensive gates.
According to the diary, Jacobus Potgieter, the laager commandant, built two gates.
These gates were intended to secure the laager properly in the event of an attack.
The Reverend also specifically mentions that the laager had been laid out in a square.
(In other words, this particular laager stood directly opposite Sooilaer on the Tugela River.)

1840
The Battle of the Makonka Hills, in which Dingane's forces were finally defeated.
According to Wikipedia, the battle at the Makonka Hills is actually known as the Battle of Maqongqa and took place on 29 January 1840.
Several sources agree to a considerable extent regarding the events leading up to the battle.
On 14 January 1840, Mpanda set out against Dingane with an impi of approximately 5,000 men.
Nongalaza kaNondela was Mpanda's chief commander. The Voortrekkers consisted of approximately 308 men and around 50 ox-wagons.
Several servants accompanied the commando.
Dingane was aware of the impending danger and sent one of his best generals, Dambuza, to negotiate for peace.
Dambuza, however, was summarily executed.
(To be continued.)

1888
Ernst Berthold Grosskopf was born.
He is remembered as a rebel during the 1914 Rebellion, as well as the author of, among other works, the book Patrys-hulle.

Wednesday, 18 October 1899
Anglo-Boer War
The eighth day of the war.
- President M.T. Steyn sent an official document to the inhabitants of Basutoland.
Among other things, he declared that the Orange Free State was not at war with Basutoland and that the commandos stationed along the borders were there solely to maintain order.
- Commandant C.J. de Villiers, together with the campaigning Field Cornet C.R. de Wet, attacked the Natal Carbineers near Bester Station.
The British forces were driven back to Ladysmith.

Wednesday, 17 October 1900
Anglo-Boer War
Day 373 of the war.
- The second of the Long Tom “Creusot” guns was destroyed with dynamite by the burghers. The pieces of the gun were thrown into the Letaba River, near Haenertsburg.
- General French arrived at Ermelo.
He had been under constant pressure from the republican forces.
- General Ben Viljoen arrived at Pietersburg.
President M.T. Steyn and General L. Botha were also there.
A war council was held to discuss the way forward.
- Commandant Gideon Scheepers and 60 burghers arrived in Philippolis.
- Brigadier-General Settle's camp was attacked during the night at Elizabethrus, north of Hoopstad. The attack was repulsed, but 16 (18) casualties were reported.
- General Liebenberg ambushed a British patrol near Frederikstad, at Rietfontein. Seven British soldiers were killed. Four soldiers were reported wounded, and another seven were captured.

Friday, 18 October 1901
Anglo-Boer War
Day 738 of the war.
- The government of the South African Republic (ZAR) was at Bankop.
- General J.C. Smuts crossed the Swartberg Mountains.
- Two “joiners” from the Christiana District Mounted Rifles were tried at Wolmaransstad. Both were found guilty and executed outside the town.

1937
The first group of veterans who had fought in the Anglo-Boer War returned to South Africa, arriving in Cape Town from Argentina.
These were veterans who had refused to sign the British oath of allegiance and had chosen to emigrate instead.

1946
The Special Service Battalion was disbanded as a unit of the Union Defence Force.
The army, air force and navy gymnasiums were established shortly afterwards.

1961
The first general election in the Republic of South Africa was held on this day.
The National Party won, securing 105 of the 160 seats.

SUNDAY MORNING DEVOTION: ¹⁸ OCT ²⁰²⁶:

📖 ⁴⁶"About the ninth hour Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?"--which means, "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" ⁵⁰And when Jesus had cried out again in a loud voice, he gave up his spirit. ⁵¹At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook and the rocks split." (Matthew 27:46,50-51)

LESSON:

I. Matthew 27:46 and 50–51 capture the final moments of Jesus on the cross—his cry of abandonment, his voluntary death, and the immediate supernatural tearing of the temple curtain.

II. Key Lessons from the Passage 

1) Jesus experienced real forsakenness so that we never have to (v. 46):
a. Jesus quotes the opening of Psalm 22. This is not mere poetry or play-acting. In bearing the sin of the world (2 Corinthians 5:21), He endured a real sense of abandonment by the Father—the judgment that sin deserves.
b. The darkness that covered the land (v. 45) underscores this spiritual reality.
c. Because the Son was forsaken in our place, those who trust Him will never be abandoned by God (Hebrews 13:5; Romans 8:38–39).
d. The cry also shows that even in deepest anguish, Jesus still addresses God as “My God,” modeling faith that clings to God when feelings of God’s presence are gone.

2) Jesus’ death was voluntary and complete (v. 50):
a. He “gave up his spirit”/“yielded up His spirit.” No one took His life from Him; He laid it down of His own accord (John 10:17–18).
b. The loud cry (elsewhere recorded as “It is finished”) signals that the work of atonement was accomplished.
c. He did not die as a defeated victim but as the One who finished the mission the Father gave Him.

3) The way to God is now open (v. 51a):
a. The massive temple curtain that separated the Holy of Holies (God’s symbolic presence) from the people was torn from top to bottom—an act of God, not of human hands. This signified that the barrier of sin had been removed.
b. Through Christ’s death, believers now have direct access to God (Hebrews 10:19–22).
c. The old sacrificial system’s exclusive inner sanctuary was rendered obsolete; the true and living way has been opened.

4) Creation itself responds to the death of the Son (v. 51b):
a. The earthquake and splitting rocks testify that this was no ordinary death.
b. The cosmos bears witness to the significance of the cross. (Matthew continues the account with opened tombs and raised saints, pointing forward to the resurrection power unleashed by Jesus’ victory over death.)

III. Core takeaways

1) Sin is so serious that it required the forsakenness of the sinless Son.
2) Salvation is finished and freely offered because Jesus willingly completed the work.
3) Access to God is no longer mediated by temple rituals or human priests but is open through Christ alone.
4) The cross is not only a human tragedy; it is a divine transaction with cosmic consequences.
5) These verses sit at the heart of the gospel: Jesus was forsaken so we could be accepted, He died so we could live, and the barrier is gone so we can come boldly to the throne of grace. (Grok.2026. Key Lessons from Matthew 27:46,50-51)

Good morning!🙏🏿

A. "Jesus was delivered over to death for our sins and was raised to life for our justification." (Romans 4:25)

B. "And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized and wash your sins away, calling on his name." (Acts 22:16)

HAVE A BLESSED FIRST DAY OF THE WEEK!

Beloved, the cross declares it finished: the forsakenness is over, the barrier is torn, and access is open. Hear the gospel, believe, repent, confess Jesus is Lord, be baptized, and live faithfully.

ii) Let us walk into this new week with confidence—Jesus was abandoned so you never will be. Come boldly. Live freely. Forgiveness of our sins is found only in Jesus Christ. God allows a U-turn. Let us keep the faith, trust, and obey Him daily. God is love! 

In the service of Christ!

text:
Fine Organics: Investing Today for Tomorrow’s Growth

Fine Organic Industries makes plant-based speciality additives used in food, plastics, cosmetics and coatings. Its expansion story begins with a simple challenge: existing factories have limited spare capacity, restricting how much additional business the company can serve.

Imagine a popular restaurant whose kitchen is already busy. More customers create growth only when the kitchen can prepare more meals. Fine Organics needs additional manufacturing space for the same reason.

Earlier investments expanded its Ambernath and Patalganga facilities. Patalganga’s second phase was commissioned in FY22. In May 2026, management expected its food-additive facility to reach full utilisation during FY27, offering scope to earn more from existing infrastructure.

The main upcoming project is the ₹700–750 crore JNPA Special Economic Zone facility in Maharashtra. Management’s May guidance targeted commissioning in H2 FY28, approximately October 2027–March 2028, compared with the earlier FY27 expectation.

Existing export production can move to JNPA, freeing older factories to serve domestic demand. However, transferring production does not itself increase group sales. Additional business must fill the enlarged manufacturing network.

Funding is progressing. Investment in the SEZ subsidiary stood at ₹192.5 crore in March 2026, followed by another ₹55 crore subscription in September. These funding amounts should not be confused with completed construction spending.

Overseas, approximately 160 acres acquired in South Carolina provide a platform for phased manufacturing expansion. Thailand offers further opportunities, while the completed acquisition of 80% of Malaysia’s Oleofine adds an established overseas business.

For investors, the financial sequence matters: construction consumes cash first; sales and profits follow later. Initial depreciation and operating expenses can weigh on returns until utilisation improves.

My assessment is that JNPA is the milestone to follow. Track construction, commissioning, additional volumes, debt and operating cash flow. Expansion creates opportunity, but attractive shareholder returns require timely execution, profitable sales and disciplined capital allocation.

🚨 AMERICANS ARE GETTING RIPPED OFF BY RESTAURANT TIP SCREENS — AND THIS CUSTOMER JUST CAUGHT ONE ON CAMERA

A customer at Texas Roadhouse noticed something seriously wrong with the suggested tip on his bill.

His total was $66. 
The screen suggested $16 for a 20% tip.

There's just one problem.

20% of $66 is $13.20.

That's an extra $2.80 the customer was being prompted to leave.

Now imagine how many people hit that button without ever checking the math.

And it gets worse.

Another customer left his waitress a massive $300 tip, only for her to return with a handwritten note asking him to pay in cash instead.

She even offered to reprint the receipt so he could remove the card tip entirely.

Now customers are questioning whether their electronic tips are actually reaching the employees who earned them.

Restaurants are already charging Americans an arm and a leg for food, then shoving tip screens in their faces like customers owe them another paycheck.

And apparently, now customers have to double check the math themselves.

Why are Americans expected to blindly hand over 20% tips when restaurants can't even make their suggested amounts add up?

text:
Given that specific context — **inherent dominance** + **a desire to draw the other to your side** — the answer sharpens considerably:

**"superiority"** is the right word, and here's why it beats the understated options:

> *"In time you will recognize my superiority."*

The seduction lives entirely in **"in time."** That phrase does the work of the invitation — it's patient, certain, and implies *you will come to me, not the other way around.* The word **superiority** then nails the dominance: it's not "merit" (which implies effort) or "standing" (which is institutional). **Superiority** in a noble's mouth is *inherent* — it's what you're born into, what the other person simply *fails to see yet.*

The full sentence reads as a **declaration wrapped in a promise**: *"I am above you. You haven't seen it yet. You will. And when you do, you'll be on my side."*

That's exactly the Malfoy-to-Potter dynamic — no anger, no pleading, just the calm certainty of someone who has already decided the outcome.

**Why not the others in this context:**

| Word | Why it falls short here |
|------|------------------------|
| **merit** | Implies *earned* worth — undermines the "inherent dominance" requirement |
| **standing** | Too institutional; sounds like a bureaucrat, not a rival |
| **worth** | Too quiet; a noble *desiring* someone wouldn't whisper |
| **preeminence** | Correct but cold — lacks the personal edge of a rivalry |

**"Superiority"** is the word that lets a character be both **dominant** and **seductive** in a single sentence, which is precisely the tone of Malfoy addressing Potter.

/me
It's a 4-panel meme series. We want each one usable independently as a meme without the others but together forming a comic:
"Superior intellect? Naturally."
"I am a Malfoy, Potter. I am superior in EVERY way."
"In time you will recognize my ____."
"I will prove it by showing you. "
So we want to avoid superiority because it's already in use in the previous panel and the one before that as "superior".

The key constraint from panel 4 is **"I will prove it by showing you"** — the word in panel 3 must be something you can *demonstrate*. That rules out abstract states like "preeminence" or "ascendancy."

**Top pick: "mastery"**

> *"In time you will recognize my mastery."*
> *"I will prove it by showing you."*

It's the most **demonstrable** word in the set — you literally *show* someone what mastery looks like. It also fits the wizard context perfectly: mastery of magic, of a situation, of yourself. It's confident without repeating "superior," and it shifts the axis from *rank* to *skill*, which makes the seduction work — he's not just saying "I'm above you," he's saying "I'm *better* at this, and you'll see."

**Why it beats the alternatives:**

| Word | Problem |
|------|---------|
| **excellence** | Works, but too broad — "proving excellence by showing" feels vague |
| **preeminence** | Formal and noble, but you can't really *show* someone your preeminence — it's a state, not a demonstration |
| **dominance** | Too aggressive; kills the seductive patience of "in time" |
| **genius** | Too casual for a Malfoy |

**The full comic reads:**

> *"Superior intellect? Naturally."*
> *"I am a Malfoy, Potter. I am superior in EVERY way."*
> *"In time you will recognize my mastery."*
> *"I will prove it by showing you."*

Each panel works standalone as a meme, and together they escalate from a dry observation → a declaration → a promise → an offer. The shift from "superior" (panels 1–2) to "mastery" (panel 3) gives the character a new dimension — he's not just born above you, he's *better* at this, and he's going to *show* you. That's the seduction.

(continued)

**INTELLIGENCE SITREP**  
**Subject: Serious Incident and Major Fire at CFB Wainwright, Alberta**  
**Date/Time of Report: ~01:30 EDT / 23:30 MT, 18 October 2026**  
**Status: Developing**

### Executive Summary

At approximately 16:00 MT on 17 October 2026, a fire was reported on the training range at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright in east-central Alberta. The incident produced both fatalities and injuries. Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed casualties but declined to release numbers, describing the situation as “very, very active and delicate” and stating he could not recall a comparable event in recent memory. The fire, driven by high winds associated with a passing cold front, crossed the base boundary and continued burning south of Township Road 44-0. No evacuation order was issued. Edmonton hospitals activated Code Orange (mass-casualty protocol) after Wainwright Health Centre was overwhelmed. The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) and RCMP are investigating. Cause remains unconfirmed; early local and media references to an explosion and possible live-fire or munitions involvement have not been officially verified.

### Background – CFB Wainwright

CFB Wainwright (3rd Canadian Division Support Base Detachment Wainwright) is one of Canada’s principal Army training bases and the primary site for live-fire and combined-arms exercises. It covers roughly 609 km² (235 sq mi), includes approximately 25 weapons ranges, and hosts the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre. Regular garrison strength is reported at ~690 military personnel and ~300 civilians, with numbers rising significantly during major exercises. The base has trained units for Korea, Afghanistan, and current NATO rotations. The range also contains shared civilian infrastructure, including roughly 180 buried natural gas wells and pipelines. Prescribed burns for fuel management are routine; a 2024 prescribed burn escaped and produced a ~600-hectare fire.

### Timeline (Mountain Time, 17 October 2026 – confirmed or widely reported)

- Earlier afternoon: Cold front passage produced wind shifts and gusts (reported up to 69 km/h locally; higher gusts recorded farther west).
- ~16:00: CAF reports fire on the range; fire extends beyond the training-area boundary. Wainwright RCMP responds to a request for assistance (“early reports were that there was a fire at a training area”).
- ~17:00–17:30: Municipal District of Wainwright notes rapid spread due to high winds; residents advised to avoid the area and keep roads clear.
- ~18:00+: CAF public statement confirms fire reported at 1600 and ongoing response. Prime Minister Mark Carney posts that a “serious incident creating a major fire” has occurred and that federal authorities are coordinating with Alberta.
- ~19:00–20:00: Fire crosses base fence; active area reported south of Township Road 44-0. Multi-jurisdictional firefighting resources engaged. STARS air ambulance aircraft noted in the area.
- ~20:00: Defence Minister McGuinty confirms fatalities and injuries. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith describes a “significant and tragic fire” affecting military personnel.
- Evening: Wainwright Health Centre overwhelmed; Edmonton activates Code Orange at Royal Alexandra and University of Alberta hospitals. Patients diverted across the city; additional medical teams mobilized. RCMP notes its initial involvement is winding down, with further details to come from CAF.
- Late evening: Saskatchewan and British Columbia offer resources. Elections Alberta closes a local advance-voting location because of the fire. No evacuation order remains in effect.

### Casualties and Medical Response

McGuinty has confirmed both fatalities and injuries. Exact numbers, identities, and conditions have not been released by official sources as of this report. A physician at Royal Alexandra Hospital (Dr. Warren Thirsk) described the patient volume as sufficient to overwhelm Edmonton itself and characterized the event as a “one in every 15 to 25-year disaster.” Wainwright’s local health facilities were described as completely overwhelmed. STARS air ambulance (from Edmonton and Saskatoon) and other aircraft movements consistent with patient transfer have been observed. Unconfirmed media and social-media reports have circulated higher casualty figures; these have not been corroborated by CAF, DND, or RCMP statements.

### Fire Status and Environmental Factors

The fire originated on the range and spread beyond the training-area boundary and base fence under strong winds. As of late evening it was being actively managed south of Township Road 44-0 by local, mutual-aid, and out-of-province resources. No civilian evacuation order was issued. Satellite heat detections (open-source analysis) suggested a narrow, wind-driven band roughly 3.5 km in length oriented west-southwest to east-northeast, though full extent remains subject to ground verification. Dry conditions and limited overnight rain prospects were noted.

### Official Response and Statements

- Prime Minister Mark Carney: Serious incident creating a major fire; thoughts with affected personnel; federal-provincial coordination.
- Defence Minister David McGuinty: Fatalities and injuries confirmed; situation active and delicate; investigation underway with CAF and RCMP; no comparable recent incident recalled.
- Chief of the Defence Staff Gen. Jennie Carignan: CAF fully engaged; priority on welfare of members, families, and community.
- Alberta Premier Danielle Smith: Significant and tragic fire affecting military personnel; close contact with federal authorities.
- Opposition and provincial leaders (including Pierre Poilievre and others) expressed support and urged prayers/resources for affected personnel and first responders.
- CAF initial statement (approx. 18:00): Fire reported on the range at 1600; extended beyond training-area boundary; emergency services responding; situation ongoing.

### Investigation and Open Questions

CAF and RCMP are investigating. Officials have not confirmed an explosion, live-fire training activity, ammunition cook-off, or interaction with range infrastructure (including natural-gas wells). When asked about munitions involvement, McGuinty did not confirm the suggestion. Lead investigative agency (RCMP, Military Police, or Canadian Forces National Investigation Service) has not been publicly specified. Specific units or exercises on the range at the time have not been identified. Further information is expected from CAF as it is confirmed.

### Analytical Notes (OSINT Assessment)

The scale of the medical response (local facility overwhelmed + Code Orange in a major urban centre + air-ambulance surge) indicates a significant casualty event, consistent with the minister’s characterization of it as outside recent experience. Occurrence on the live-fire range during a period of high winds raises the possibility of training-related ignition or secondary effects, but this remains unconfirmed. The presence of buried natural-gas infrastructure on the range is a known factor in range-management planning; any linkage is speculative pending official findings. Impact on ongoing or imminent training cycles (including NATO readiness) cannot yet be assessed. Information is incomplete and the situation remains dynamic.

**Current Status (as of report time):** Fire response ongoing; casualties confirmed but not quantified; investigation active; no evacuation order; public updates to follow from CAF/DND.

This compilation is drawn exclusively from contemporaneous public statements by Canadian federal, provincial, and local authorities, CAF releases, and contemporaneous reporting by major Canadian and international outlets. It will be superseded by subsequent official releases.

(End of SITREP)

text:
🚨 BREAKING: Canada's defence minister confirms people were killed and injured at one of the country's busiest army training bases. He won't say how many yet. Here's what's on the record about CFB Wainwright. 🇨🇦🔥

📊 The numbers
• Dead or injured: not released. McGuinty called it "a very active and delicate situation" (CP24/CTV)
• Gusts up to 100 km/h (about 62 mph) across parts of Alberta pushed the fire past the base fence (Global News, MD of Wainwright)
• 2 STARS air ambulances sent, from Saskatoon and Edmonton (CTV)
• About 200 km southeast of Edmonton
• 11,500+ X posts on Wainwright in about 4 hours (X post counts)

🗣️ What people are saying
• PM Carney: a "serious incident creating a major fire." Premier Smith: "significant and tragic," affecting "many" military personnel
• MP Dane Lloyd says he's hearing of "significant casualties" after an explosion
• Premiers Moe (Sask.) and Eby (B.C.) have offered help; Saskatchewan has already sent crews
• Online, some are already blaming Ottawa, while others say it's far too early to blame anyone

✅ The facts
• McGuinty: "fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base." He said he can't recall an incident like it in recent memory (AP: https://t.co/CZZCuvFu4c)
• The MD of Wainwright says the fire crossed the base fence and is burning south of Township Road 44-0. People are told to avoid the area (CBC: https://t.co/oBK0x5zQku)
• No evacuation order for residents as of 7:30 PM MT. Elections Alberta closed the Wainwright Communiplex advance poll (CP24: https://t.co/wuqrvoFSZR)

❓ Not verified yet
• What caused it. Several outlets report an explosion, but the minister's own words were "an incident," and he wouldn't confirm whether weapons or ammunition were involved
• How many people died or were hurt. Any number you see right now is not official
• Who the victims are. Next of kin come first

🤔 Why early numbers mislead
In the first hours of a disaster, casualty figures usually come from people relaying what they've heard, and they often change a lot. The fire and the incident that started it are also two separate questions. High winds explain how the fire spread, not what set it off.

Prompt :

Style: Hyper-realistic, nostalgic Japanese school home video recorded on an early-2000s consumer digital camcorder.

CORE CONCEPT

A Japanese high school girl spending an ordinary school day, casually recorded by her closest friend. Nothing is staged. Her expressions and movements are natural, quiet, and spontaneous. The video should feel like a real memory recovered years later.

CHARACTER CONSISTENCY

The same Japanese high school girl throughout all six scenes. Friendly, approachable face, realistic skin texture, short black bob haircut with a small silver hairpin above her right ear. White short-sleeved school shirt, maroon ribbon, gray pleated skirt, white socks, and indoor school slippers. Outside school, she wears simple white sneakers and carries the same navy school bag.

Maintain identical facial features, hairstyle, body proportions, uniform, and belongings in every scene.

TIMED SCRIPT

SCENE 1 — 0:00–0:03 | Morning Classroom

A lived-in Japanese public high school classroom in soft morning sunlight. The girl enters carrying her navy school bag, notices her friend recording, and gives a small sleepy smile. She places her bag beside her desk and sits down naturally.

Camera: Handheld medium shot, slightly imperfect framing, gentle natural shake.

HARD CUT.

SCENE 2 — 0:03–0:06 | Window-Side Desk

She sits beside the classroom window and opens her notebook. A light breeze gently lifts one page. She presses it down with her fingers, glances toward the camera, and smiles softly before looking back at her notebook.

Camera: Casual handheld framing from the neighboring desk. Natural window light and realistic paper movement.

HARD CUT.

SCENE 3 — 0:06–0:09 | Lunch Break

In the school courtyard, she sits on a simple bench holding a sandwich wrapped in paper. She takes a bite, notices the camera, and playfully offers the sandwich toward her friend. Her eyes narrow naturally as she smiles.

Camera: Medium-wide home-video shot. A few students and green trees remain softly visible in the background.

HARD CUT.

SCENE 4 — 0:09–0:12 | School Corridor

She walks down a quiet school corridor with her school bag over one shoulder. Someone behind the camera says something indistinct. She turns her head, laughs naturally for a moment, then continues walking. The camera adjusts slightly to keep her in frame.

Camera: Handheld follow shot at normal walking speed. No stabilization or dramatic movement.

HARD CUT.

SCENE 5 — 0:12–0:15 | The Last Moments in Class

The classroom is almost empty after school. Warm late-afternoon sunlight falls across the desks. She stands beside her window-side desk, rests one hand on its edge, and quietly looks outside at the trees. She turns toward the camera and gives a gentle, unposed smile.

Camera: Mostly stationary handheld medium shot with slight natural movement.

HARD CUT.

SCENE 6 — 0:15–0:20 | Walking Home

Outside the school gate, she walks away along a quiet Japanese residential street in soft golden evening light. The camera follows a few steps behind. She notices her friend has slowed down, turns around, and gives a small, genuine wave with a warm smile. She turns back and continues walking until she moves toward the far end of the street.

The camera stops following and remains pointed at the quiet street for one extra moment. We hear her fading footsteps, a few birds, and a gentle breeze. The recording abruptly cuts off at exactly 20 seconds without a fade.

CAMERA AND VISUAL STYLE

Early-2000s consumer digital camcorder footage. Slight handheld shake, imperfect framing, mild autofocus adjustments, subtle digital noise, slightly soft image details, muted colors, imperfect white balance, and natural exposure fluctuations.

Natural available light only. Realistic skin pores, individual hair strands, and natural facial expressions. Ordinary Japanese school architecture and authentic background activity.

text:
44. The Hunt for Red October, by Tom Clancy
5/5 (obviously)

I said a while back that I was thinking of doing a comprehensive read of Tom Clancy’s novels. Well, the time is now!

If I can offer an anecdote from my life that I think is informative here… when I was in the USAF I spent a fair bit of time on midshift, or as civvies might put it, graveyard shift. One of the main things I did was service the liquid oxygen systems on the aircraft. You’d have a bit of time during this process where you’re waiting for the tank to fill up, so when I was servicing the entire squadron‘s worth of jets I’d usually bring a paperback and read while this was going on. One day I’m reading Starship Troopers while I work. Another guy sees me and says “don’t you know there’s a movie of that now?” I go “of course, but the book is a lot different from the movie. There’s a lot more going on in this.” He had no idea. Well… this is like that. Yes, there’s a movie. Yes, it’s a great movie. But my goodness is there so much more going on in this. 

So this is obviously Clancy’s first novel, about a Soviet captain who seeks to use his command of a brand new ballistic missile submarine with a revolutionary stealthy drive system to defect to the United States, as well as the efforts by the Soviet Navy to prevent this and the CIA and U.S./Royal Navies to facilitate this. And my goodness is it a great novel. 

There’s a lot to love here. In particular for me there’s even a part where A-10s launch a brilliantly effective mock attack run on a Soviet battlecruiser. I loved that part. There’s a ton of stuff for military buffs, Soviet/communism disrespecters, fans of spy thrillers, etc., and it also introduces the character Jack Ryan. In a lot of ways too it seems like what nowadays we’d call competence porn. A lot of it is just people who are really good at their jobs doing those jobs very effectively. And my goodness is the writing great. I read most of the penultimate chapter today (which correlates to the scene in the movie where the Soviet Alfa-class attack sub confronts the Red October and USS Dallas, though in the book the USS Pogy is also involved), and it was edge of my seat stuff. The suspense was so masterfully done. 

Suffice it to say I LOVED this book. I can’t recommend it enough. I seem to recall trying to read it once when I was in my early teens but I didn’t really have the attention span for it at the time. Now, though? Oh boy. Now I’m basically the target audience. Haven’t watched the movie in ages either, so I might have to. I was that weird kid where in junior high it was my favorite movie. I’d honestly like to see a more faithful adaptation of the book but that would take a limited series or something at least. 

Anyway, great book. Check it out if you haven’t. 

Oh, and how weird is it that the political officer aboard the Red October was named Putin? I know we joke about Tom Clancy being prophetic but wow. 

Also, know that in my head I heard dialogue in the voices of the actors (Sean Connery for Ramius, Tim Curry for Dr. Petrov, Scott Glenn for Bart Mancuso, of course James Earl Jones for Admiral Greer, etc…)

Entering Cignetti’s second season at Indiana, his high school class ranked 46th nationally in the 247Sports Composite, and his transfer class ranked 25th.

Stein’s FIRST transfer class at Kentucky ranked 10th nationally, with six four-star transfers compared with three in Cignetti’s second class....before Stein ever coached a game as a head coach.  

Rankings aren’t guarantees, and class size influences them. But Stein demonstrated he could attract talented transfers before coaching a game at Kentucky. Imagine how much stronger his pitch could be this offseason.

When he arrived, he was selling a vision. Now recruits can watch that vision taking shape. They can see his offense, transfers contributing, and a team winning meaningful games.....including in Norman tonight.

Kentucky has talented players, but Stein is producing these results before having multiple recruiting cycles to build the roster and depth he wants. That should appeal to players who believe they could help this team take another step.  Depth is the problem UK has this season.... and it's showing on the defensive side of the ball.   

For a strong transfer, Kentucky could offer SEC competition, national exposure and a realistic opportunity to earn significant playing time EARLY. Combine those opportunities with a staff showing it can use players effectively, and that becomes a compelling pitch.

The atmosphere matters, too. From the outside, these players seem to love playing for this staff and being around each other. There’s energy and confidence around the program. Recruits will hear directly from those players when they visit, and enthusiastic players can be a coach’s best recruiters.

Meanwhile, Stein already has an encouraging group of high school commitments for his first full recruiting cycle. Those commitments still have to become signees, but the foundation was developing before this season’s success strengthened his recruiting message.... Landing Hall would be huge, and its likely to happen.....

The next step is keeping the productive core together and adding transfers who address specific weaknesses. That was an important part of Cignetti’s approach: retain good players, find experienced additions who fit, and build on what already works.

Kentucky will need competitive financial offers, good evaluations and strong retention. More talent alone doesn’t guarantee improvement....but Stein's staff seems to be really great at evaluating talent....and they seem to be willing to walk away if the price gets to high.   And there is gonna be more money coming his way.....

But Stein recruited well before he had results here. Now he has results, an appealing team atmosphere, promising high school commitments and opportunities for newcomers to contribute.

There’s a credible path from this year’s success to a stronger roster next year..... and that is potentially something Kentucky can sustain.

text:
Trust the science you say?  

On December 14, 1799, the day he died, George Washington was bled several times as treatment for a severe throat and airway infection. 

He had been outdoors in cold, wet weather the day before and woke around 2 a.m. with difficulty breathing, a sore throat, and trouble speaking or swallowing. Before doctors arrived, he asked an overseer, George Rawlins, to bleed him.   

Rawlins removed about 12–14 ounces; Washington asked for more, and Martha Washington intervened to stop it.  

Once physicians were present—primarily Dr. James Craik, with Drs. Elisha Cullen Dick and Gustavus Richard Brown—further bleedings followed through the day. Contemporary and later accounts commonly total the removals at more than 80 ounces (roughly 2.4 liters, often estimated at about 40 percent of his blood volume) over roughly 12 hours, in four sessions.   

Some medical reviews note that the exact total is not fully certain from the primary documents and place the clearly recorded amount lower (at least roughly 44–46 ounces), while still agreeing that the bleedings were large and repeated. 

Dick objected to the last major bleeding, arguing Washington needed his strength, but was overruled.  The doctors diagnosed “cynanche trachealis” (inflammation of the upper airway). 

Modern interpretations usually favor acute bacterial epiglottitis or a similar rapidly progressive throat infection. 

Other treatments included blistering agents, an enema, and purgatives such as calomel and tartar emetic.   

Washington died that evening, around 10–10:30 p.m., at Mount Vernon. 

Bloodletting was standard practice under the humoral medicine of the time; it did not help and almost certainly weakened him. 

The mistake people make with their doctors when blindly accepting their treatment is that they  believe that the years of classroom training and years of residency rounding in hospitals equates with a significant amount of real world knowledge that is both effective and safe

- the knowledge maybe there, but these programs offer little to no encouragement to actually think - they are merely seeing and memorizing in order to pass their board examinations 

- tests that require the ability to recall but never to think.   

Consider - if the mountain of “knowledge” was never based in true scientific investigation but rather something that was influenced by profit or correlation, the resultant product that we as physicians “sell” to our patients is suspect 

-without a thinking mind, we may actually end up hurting our patients and blaming any subsequent observations of adverse effects on something we are comfortable in assigning blame to...

- which is usually explained as part of the disease process itself and never an iatrogenic response because we are too narcissistic to understand or accept that our treatment could have caused harm. 

When you hear someone talk about the science, consider: doctors truly thought they were helping George Washington with what we now define as barbaric treatment.   

That was the accepted science.  

I am sure, that our future generations will look back on our treatments of today and forever wonder why we believed in our “science.”

Do no harm.

text:
💰 WHO GETS THE CHECK —
Help, Control, and the Bill 🧾
🧩 THE INTENT QUESTION ▸ ▸ ▸ 📖 Post 8 OF 17 
https://t.co/1MOXvyl79T

✅ Unmarried mothers gave birth to 69.3 percent of Black American babies in 2023, according to the CDC. For white babies it was 26.8 percent. In 1965, a Labor Department report treated a Black rate of 23.6 percent as a case for national action.

The white rate today is higher than the one that alarmed Washington then.

▸ ▸ ▸

That single comparison does not settle anything. It does change the question.

The claim this post tests is the most explosive one in the series: that welfare was built to destroy the Black family. It is made sincerely by many Americans, including prominent Black scholars. It deserves a real test, not a dismissal and not a slogan.

The test has three parts. What the program's rules did. What the data shows happened. And whether anyone meant it.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE CASE FOR YES, AT FULL STRENGTH

The strongest version of the claim does not need a secret memo. It rests on dates.

📊 The economist Thomas Sowell, writing in National Review on November 18, 2014, pointed out that "the poverty rate among blacks fell from 87 percent in 1940 to 47 percent by 1960." That is before the Great Society, and before welfare reached most Black families in the South. His figures use a different measure from the official Census series, which begins at 55.1 percent in 1959.

He also argued that most Black children were being raised in two-parent families in 1960, nearly a century after slavery, and that thirty years into the welfare state the great majority were not. The piece's summary line put it in one sentence: current problems "owe more to the Great Society than to slavery."

📊 In 1984 the political scientist Charles Murray made the mechanism argument in Losing Ground. His case was that the rule changes of the 1960s made it rational, in the short run, for a poor young couple not to marry and for a poor young man not to take a low-wage job, because the household did better on aid without him.

And the design facts from earlier in this series back the mechanism.

✅ AFDC paid when a father was absent. Alabama cut off Sylvester Smith over a man in the house. Two-parent coverage was not required nationwide until 1988. Moynihan's own Labor Department found that, starting in 1960, welfare cases stopped tracking jobs.

You do not need intent to cause damage. A program that pays for absence can produce absence whether or not anyone wanted it to.

That is the strongest honest form of the argument. Now the data it has to survive.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE BIRTH NUMBERS

The share of babies born outside marriage is a ratio. It can rise because more unmarried women have children, or because fewer women marry. Those are very different stories.

✅ CDC data on the birth rate per 1,000 unmarried women show the Black rate falling from 95.5 in 1970 to 59.6 in 2015, a drop of about 38 percent. Over the same years the rate for white women, a CDC category that includes Hispanic women, rose from 13.9 to 40.4.

🔒 Unmarried Black women were having children at a far lower rate in 2015 than in 1970. The share of Black births outside marriage rose anyway, because marriage itself fell.

That is not what a benefit that rewards unmarried births would be expected to produce on its own. It is what a collapse in marriage produces. The question becomes what drove the collapse in marriage, and whether welfare was a large part of it.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE POVERTY NUMBERS

✅ Census figures put the Black poverty rate at 55.1 percent in 1959. By 1973 it was 31.4 percent.

Then it stopped. It was 32.5 percent in 1980 and 31.9 percent in 1990. It fell to 22.5 percent in 2000, rose to 27.4 percent in 2010, and reached a record low of 17.1 percent in 2022. It was 18.4 percent in 2024.

Both sides read these numbers as proof.

Critics point to the seventeen flat years, 1973 to 1990, when welfare was at its largest and Black poverty did not move, and to the sharp fall that came after the 1996 reform and the boom of the late 1990s.

Defenders point to the total. From 1959 to 2022 the Black poverty rate fell by 38 points, about 69 percent, during the decades the programs existed.

Neither reading, on its own, proves what caused what.

▸ ▸ ▸

WHAT THE RESEARCH FOUND

📊 In 1998 the economist Robert Moffitt reviewed 68 studies for the National Research Council. His summary was that "a majority of the studies find a significant effect of welfare," raising fertility and lowering marriage. Many others found no significant effect. Some of the effects found were modest next to other influences, and some were sizable. Using changes within states over time, a method many researchers consider more credible, the effects were larger for Black women.

He also noted a problem for the main-cause theory. Nonmarital childbearing kept rising through the 1980s and 1990s while "welfare benefits have been falling over that period."

📊 The 1996 reform then ran the experiment in reverse. Congress added time limits and work requirements and let benefits shrink. A National Bureau of Economic Research working paper by the economists Ted Joyce, Robert Kaestner and colleagues found little evidence that the reform changed nonmarital births.

📊 In 1987 the sociologist William Julius Wilson offered a different main cause in The Truly Disadvantaged. As factory jobs left the cities, the number of employed Black men a woman could realistically marry fell. On that account, joblessness drove down marriage, and welfare was a smaller factor.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE CASE FOR NO

Put the strongest version of the other side on the scale.

The rise in Black nonmarital births began before welfare opened to most Black families in the South, as Post 6 showed. The same rise then happened among white Americans, whose welfare use was far lower. It kept going while real benefits fell. It did not reverse when welfare was cut in 1996.

A program can push in a direction without being the reason things moved. On the data, welfare looks like one push among several, alongside the loss of urban jobs, the national decline of marriage in every group, and changes that had nothing to do with government at all.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE INTENT

Which leaves the word in the title.

There is a more careful version of the question. Could good intent and control have existed at the same time? They could, and the record shows it. Just not in the form the popular claim says.

✅ Control is documented, in writing. Southern states used welfare rules to keep Black families off the rolls, as Post 6 showed. Alabama stated in court that its rule was meant to discourage "illicit sexual relationships." Andrew Johnson wrote that federal aid to freed people could be used for political ends. Those are control, and they are on paper.

❌ What is not on paper is a plan to use welfare to break up Black families. No law, regulation, memo, recording or testimony from anyone in a position to know has surfaced showing that goal. The one quote offered for it, the 200-year sentence in Post 7, rests on a single uncorroborated memory.

▸ ▸ ▸

THE VERDICT, TIER BY TIER

▸ ✅ The program's rules rewarded a father's absence. For fifty-three years, states were not required to aid poor children whose unemployed father stayed home.

▸ ✅ The rise in Black births outside marriage began before the welfare expansion, while most Southern Black families were shut out of welfare.

▸ 📊 Welfare had some effect on marriage and childbearing. Most studies find one. Its size is uncertain.

▸ ⚖️ Welfare was the main cause. Disputed. The same trend hit groups with far less welfare use, continued as benefits fell, and did not reverse after 1996.

▸ ❌ Welfare was designed to destroy the Black family. No evidence of that intent exists in the record.

▸ ✅ Welfare rules were used to exclude and police Black families, documented state by state. That is control, in a different form than the claim says.

💡 The bottom line: the design was harmful, the effect was real but smaller than the slogan, and the intent that is documented was control by keeping families out, not a plot to break them up once they were in.

▸ ▸ ▸

In 1996 Congress decided the design itself was the problem and tore it up.

It kept the money, handed it to the states as a block grant, and left Washington without the power to measure how much of it was paid out wrong. In one of those states, some of it went to a volleyball facility.

✂️ Next: the 1996 welfare law, a block grant that lost half its value, and the Mississippi case in which welfare money was directed to projects that had nothing to do with the poor.

📖 Post 8 of 17

text:
My Fellow Citizens of the Free World, and especially those who yet retain the name and spirit of a free people,

I have read the account of the troubles that now afflict France with a heavy heart, and with that same sober attention I once gave to the disorders that threatened our own infant republic. Nations, like men, are not exempt from the consequences of their own choices. Where a people cease to insist upon the supremacy of their own laws, the unity of their customs, and the fidelity of those who enter their borders, the bonds of society loosen, and authority itself becomes a shadow.

It was ever my conviction that a free government rests upon the character of its citizens. We admitted strangers to our shores, yet we required of them that they cast off former allegiances and adopt the principles of our Constitution, the language of our laws, and the habits of ordered liberty. Those who came merely to transplant the disorders of the places they left were not welcomed as brethren, but regarded as a danger to the common peace. A republic that cannot distinguish between the friend who seeks to share its burdens and the guest who would remake its house after his own fashion will soon find its foundations undermined.

The scenes you describe, of authority withdrawn from whole districts, of public monuments defaced, of the instruments of order held in contempt, are not the ordinary complaints of youth or the transient grievances of a single season. They are the natural fruits of a policy that has, for many years, preferred the appearance of liberality to the substance of cohesion. When the rulers of a nation spend their treasure and their credit upon measures that enlarge the number of those who feel no obligation to its ancient institutions, they purchase for themselves a temporary quiet at the price of future strength. The public debt and the public disorder are but two faces of the same neglect.

I do not pretend that every stranger is an enemy, nor that every native is a patriot. Virtue and vice are not confined to birthplace. Yet history, both ancient and modern, teaches that a people divided by irreconcilable habits, languages, and loyalties cannot long maintain a free government. Faction is the mortal disease of republics, and when that faction is nourished by the very policies of the state, the remedy becomes more difficult with every year that passes.

To the leaders of France, and to those of every nation that has opened its gates without a corresponding demand for assimilation, I would offer the counsel I once gave my own countrymen: guard with jealous care the purity of your public morals, the integrity of your borders, and the supremacy of your laws. Do not suffer the temporary interests of party, or the fashion of the day, to persuade you that a people may renounce its own character and yet retain its liberty. The experiment of a free government is not easily repeated, and once the common confidence that binds a nation is broken, no proclamation or ministry can restore it.

Let those who still love their country act with prudence and firmness. Restore the authority of the law where it has been surrendered. Require of every inhabitant the same duties and the same loyalty that you demand of your own sons. Prefer the solid advantages of a united people to the vain hopes of a heterogeneous multitude. For in the end, a nation that will not defend its own inheritance will find that it has nothing left to bequeath.

I remain, with the respect due to every sincere lover of order and liberty,
G. Washington

My Fellow Citizens of the Free World, and especially those who yet retain the name and spirit of a free people,

I have read the account of the troubles that now afflict France with a heavy heart, and with that same sober attention I once gave to the disorders that threatened our own infant republic. Nations, like men, are not exempt from the consequences of their own choices. Where a people cease to insist upon the supremacy of their own laws, the unity of their customs, and the fidelity of those who enter their borders, the bonds of society loosen, and authority itself becomes a shadow.

It was ever my conviction that a free government rests upon the character of its citizens. We admitted strangers to our shores, yet we required of them that they cast off former allegiances and adopt the principles of our Constitution, the language of our laws, and the habits of ordered liberty. 

Those who came merely to transplant the disorders of the places they left were not welcomed as brethren, but regarded as a danger to the common peace. A republic that cannot distinguish between the friend who seeks to share its burdens and the guest who would remake its house after his own fashion will soon find its foundations undermined.

The scenes you describe, of authority withdrawn from whole districts, of public monuments defaced, of the instruments of order held in contempt, are not the ordinary complaints of youth or the transient grievances of a single season. They are the natural fruits of a policy that has, for many years, preferred the appearance of liberality to the substance of cohesion. 

When the rulers of a nation spend their treasure and their credit upon measures that enlarge the number of those who feel no obligation to its ancient institutions, they purchase for themselves a temporary quiet at the price of future strength. The public debt and the public disorder are but two faces of the same neglect.

I do not pretend that every stranger is an enemy, nor that every native is a patriot. Virtue and vice are not confined to birthplace. Yet history, both ancient and modern, teaches that a people divided by irreconcilable habits, languages, and loyalties cannot long maintain a free government. 

Faction is the mortal disease of republics, and when that faction is nourished by the very policies of the state, the remedy becomes more difficult with every year that passes.

To the leaders of France, and to those of every nation that has opened its gates without a corresponding demand for assimilation, I would offer the counsel I once gave my own countrymen: guard with jealous care the purity of your public morals, the integrity of your borders, and the supremacy of your laws. *Trump signs Executive Order waiving sanctions against Russia*

President Donald Trump signed an executive order Friday waiving a sweeping sanctions package against Russia, citing national interest, just two days before it was due to take effect.

The order targets legislation named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, who championed the effort before his unexpected death in July. Trump signed the bill last month. It imposes tariffs and sanctions on Russian exports and leaders to weaken Russia’s war machine in Ukraine, targets the world’s five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, and extends sanctions against Iran.

The waiver offers economic relief to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Earlier this month, Trump announced the U.S. would import Russian diesel to lower energy prices, drawing condemnation from Democrats and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Trump did not explain the national interest behind Friday’s decision but said he had submitted a certification to Congress that the waiver served U.S. interests.

Trump faces pressure over diesel prices ahead of next month’s midterms, with the cost of living a top voter concern. Russian diesel supplies could ease prices but effectively align Washington with Moscow.

Since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the U.S. and European allies have largely supported Kyiv, though tensions have grown under Trump, who has publicly blamed Zelensky for failing to reach a settlement.

text:
India’s Statecraft in Great Power Competition

India occupies a distinctive position in an increasingly contested international order. The United States, China, Europe and Russia each present opportunities for cooperation, alongside dependencies and strategic constraints that New Delhi must manage.

READ FULL ARTICLE HERE:https://t.co/HLggPtcsqe

The challenge is not simply to maintain relationships with competing powers. It is to ensure that none of those relationships compromises India's freedom to make independent decisions.

With Washington, India can deepen defence, technology and Indo-Pacific cooperation while managing disagreements over trade and other interests. With Beijing, it must compete while addressing unresolved border tensions and reducing vulnerabilities arising from economic dependence. Europe offers opportunities in trade, technology, capital and supply chains. Russia remains relevant to India's energy and defence interests, even as Moscow's closer relationship with Beijing and the risks of concentrated dependencies complicate the equation.

India's strategic options extend beyond these four. Japan, the Gulf, Iran and the wider Global South provide additional relationships through which New Delhi can expand its choices without assuming that these partners form a unified bloc.

Yet diplomatic flexibility alone cannot guarantee strategic autonomy.

A country's ability to withstand external pressure depends on its domestic foundations: productive capacity, advanced manufacturing, technological depth, defence preparedness and economic resilience. Without these capabilities, diplomatic choices may exist on paper while remaining difficult to exercise in practice.

This is where the distinction between grand strategy and statecraft becomes important. Grand strategy establishes long-term objectives. Statecraft advances national interests as circumstances change, adapting to opportunities and constraints without abandoning those objectives.

India does not need every major power to share its vision. Nor must cooperation with one power imply permanent alignment against another. Interests may converge without requiring coordinated strategies.

The test of India's rise is therefore not whether it can dictate the choices of other powers. It is whether it can preserve its own freedom of action while navigating their competing ambitions.

India need not determine every other power's choices. It must ensure that no other power can determine India's.

— Strategic Crossroads

❗️The No Kings protests of 17 October across the United States reflect growing opposition to Donald Trump’s concentration of executive power and the weakening of democratic checks and balances. Their significance extends beyond domestic politics: they expose a contradiction at the heart of US global leadership.

For decades, Washington has urged other countries to respect the rule of law, institutional independence and democratic accountability, while frequently supporting allied governments whose practices fall short of these standards. Strategic interests have often taken precedence over democratic principles, particularly when authoritarian partners serve US security objectives.

Today, the problem is increasingly visible within the United States itself. Confrontations with the judiciary, pressure on independent institutions and the use of executive authority to pursue political objectives raise questions about the consistency of the democratic standards Washington promotes abroad.

This domestic shift also has international consequences. Allied governments and US-backed political forces operating in environments of weak institutional accountability have incentives to adopt similar practices when they perceive that executive power faces fewer constraints from law, parliament or public opinion. This conduct weakens the credibility of its democratic message and offers political cover to leaders who disregard institutional limits.

The result is a wider crisis of accountability. When the leading power treats international law as negotiable and domestic checks as obstacles, the distinction between rules-based governance and rule by executive preference becomes harder to defend. The No Kings protests therefore raise a question that extends far beyond American politics: who holds power accountable when those claiming to defend the international order begin to undermine its underlying principles?

And that would have become an issue for NATO to address

Instead Ukraine chose NOT to join NATO

The 2010 Non-Aligned Policy: On June 3, 2010, the Ukrainian parliament passed a law submitted by pro-Russian President Viktor Yanukovych that formally rejected NATO membership and established a non-aligned status, banning military bloc membership while allowing cooperation.

Post-2014 Shift: Following Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea and backing of separatists in Donbas in 2014, Ukrainian political consensus and public opinion shifted decisively toward NATO integration, culminating in constitutional amendments in 2019 and a formal application for accelerated accession in September 2022 after the full-scale invasion

2022: Following Russia's full-scale invasion, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy formally requested accelerated NATO accession, reiterating the request later that year

2023–2024: NATO removed the MAP requirement at the Vilnius Summit and described Ukraine's path to membership as "irreversible" at the Washington Summit, while noting an invitation would only be extended when conditions are met.

NATO’s official stance from the 2023 Vilnius Summit and the 2024 Washington Summit outlines that an invitation will be extended to Ukraine when all Allied nations achieve consensus and specific baseline conditions are met.
These requirements fall into several distinct categories:

1. Political, Institutional, and Governance Reforms

Ukraine must continue to demonstrate progress on comprehensive democratic, economic, and security sector reforms. Managed and assessed through an adapted Annual National Programme (aANP), these conditions specifically emphasize:
• Democratic governance and strengthening the rule of law.
• Fighting systemic corruption.
• Modernizing and establishing democratic oversight over the security and defense forces.

2. Military Interoperability

Ukraine must show substantial progress in aligning its military capabilities with Western standards. This involves adopting NATO-standard equipment, doctrine, operational procedures, and command structures to ensure its armed forces can seamlessly integrate and contribute to alliance security.

3. Resolution of Territorial Conflicts

In accordance with the foundational principles of NATO enlargement (such as those outlined in the 1949 Washington Treaty), a candidate country is expected to resolve international or territorial disputes by peaceful means.
While not explicitly named as a formal "veto," alliance diplomats and member states (such as the United States and Germany) have repeatedly noted that Ukraine cannot join while actively engaged in an armed conflict or harboring unresolved border disputes. This condition exists to prevent the immediate triggering of NATO's Article 5 collective defense clause, which could draw the entire alliance into an all-out war with Russia. Clear demarcation of territory is required to define exactly where alliance security guarantees would apply.  POTUS Donald Trump sought to negotiate a peace deal that was not successful 

4. Unanimous Allied Agreement

Ultimately, the primary political condition is the consensus of all member states. NATO operates on unanimity, meaning an invitation cannot be formalized until every single member country formally agrees that Ukraine has met the criteria and that its accession will enhance Euro-Atlantic security.

text:
Groks Response to: Which Ukrainian Oligarch paid Laura Loomer…

Rinat Akhmetov (Ukraine’s richest oligarch, owner of the DTEK energy company via SCM Holdings).

This comes from claims by Ukrainian journalist Diana Panchenko (widely described as pro-Russian; she has been investigated by Ukrainian authorities on related charges and her channel has faced restrictions). She alleged that Akhmetov paid Loomer roughly $2–3 million for her July 2026 trip to Ukraine. The claim was amplified on social media and by outlets like EADaily, tying it to Loomer’s visit to DTEK facilities (where she was photographed in company gear), meetings that included figures linked to Akhmetov’s circle, and her broader shift toward supporting Ukraine.
Key context and counterclaims:
•Loomer has repeatedly denied receiving any foreign money or being paid for the trip. She said she covered her own travel, with private American donors only helping with security due to threats, and that she received no payment from Ukraine or anyone else. She has offered to sign an affidavit or take a lie detector test on this.
•Mainstream reporting (AP, Washington Post, etc.) notes the trip, her interviews (including with Zelenskyy), her visit to DTEK, and her public reversal of earlier anti-Ukraine views, while reporting her denials of being paid. No independent confirmation of an Akhmetov payment has surfaced in these accounts.
•Akhmetov/DTEK is a major private energy player that has received reconstruction-related aid and has hosted various visitors; the specific “paid $3 million” figure remains an allegation from Panchenko without publicly detailed financial evidence in the available reporting.

In short, the oligarch named in the circulating claim is Rinat Akhmetov. The allegation is unverified, originates from a contested source, and is flatly denied by Loomer.

Here is why this matters for your hard-earned money in India:

• The Value Math: Offline store managers have aggressive monthly targets. When you stack festival bank offers with corporate discounts and old phone exchange values, local retail often beats online net pricing by straight thousands of rupees.
